open_obligations: Note that Buhl et al. state a requirement, not a proof that debate tolerates bounded systematic error.
Check whether 'washes out over training' corresponds to Brown-Cohen et al.'s stochastic-oracle Theorem 6.2.
Check how systematic error would be measured.
in.other_title: Good human input: bounded systematic error of human judges and their simulation
in.rationale: Brown-Cohen et al. ask whether debate results extend to oracles that err on some queries. Buhl et al. argue random judge errors should wash out over training, so the concern is systematic error, and require bounded systematic error of simulated human input with respect to reality and of the simulation with respect to humans; this is a stated requirement in a safety-case sketch, not a theorem.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: which kinds of human-judge error debate must tolerate, in a debate-based alignment safety case

text: The authors note that human judgement is fallible and practical oversight trains reward models to approximate it, so the verifier's oracle is likely flawed; Theorem 6.2 only partly addresses this by allowing stochastic answers with a constant advantage over random guessing. They ask whether the results extend to oracles that give incorrect answers on some subset of queries, such as an arbitrary subset of limited size, or arbitrary errors on a randomly selected subset.
title: Open: debate with a flawed human-judgement oracle that errs on some queries
